text: The Jade Blood Taoists of Weng Chang's Spirit Hall answer only to the summons of the Jade Court. They study the elemental wind of life in pursuit of mastery over desire.
The Jade Lion's fierce gaze subdues evil spirits; standing proud before the ranks, its majesty commands awe, and no demon or fiend dares draw near.
The ink lions guard the temple gates with solemn dignity; when chaos and rebellion arise and the people suffer, they follow the sovereign's decree to sweep away evil and corruption.

The Cassia Confidants are an intelligence agency directly under Hong Ying's command. Their garments are dyed entirely black, with silver thread embroidering the collars in patterns of silver luan birds and cassia trees; they have won glorious victories deep behind enemy lines.

[Pale Moon's Dark Crow] Hong Ying carries the mysterious blood of the shadow dragon and possesses extraordinary talent, held in high regard by the Moon Empress. He commands the Cassia Confidants, serving as the capable right hand of [Jade Dragon] Yuan Bo, active deep behind enemy lines.

The Black Jade Crow Wardens were personally crafted by the Moon Empress using the divination of wind, serving as the sharp eyes and shadow blades of the Celestial Empire of Cathay, obeying the commands of [Jade Dragon] Yuan Bo and [Pale Moon's Dark Crow] Hong Ying.

The oldest and greatest creation of the Triceratops God possesses a ferocious temperament beyond compare; only those chosen by Itza may approach it. Its dreadful great bow and blowdarts strike down enemies amid rolling thunder.
The largest and most bloodthirsty of ripperdactyls, their razor-sharp claws can decapitate enemies, and their furious assaults leave scattered entrails and severed limbs in their wake.
An experimental jetpack is more than sufficient to withstand the recoil of an Irondrake rifle - these grizzled veterans call themselves 'Dragons' as they roast Skaven and Greenskins alike.
These elite guards ride rare black mountain goats - swing this hammer down, and either the enemy's skull shatters or the wielder's arm dislocates.
'Ironflame?' What engineer would dream up such a rebellious name for a new weapon? Surely these little goats aren't just blackened by gunpowder smoke...
Docile goats are a vital source of meat for the Dwarfs, but the troublemakers of the pen get sent to the battlefield before they ever reach the kitchen.
A few tankards of Bergmann ale can grant remarkable strength, but I say: Dawi! Aim carefully and don't hit my beer barrel!
Oh, these Slayers already jump higher than most of their kin, but bragging they can cut down a dragon? Valaya preserve us!
Remember, lad, when you spot a goblin on patrol, be patient and lie in wait - there's likely a whole horde of greenskins behind him. - 'Modin Whitebeard,' Longbeard warrior
Grimnir is the god of war, who protected the fledgling Dwarf race from monstrous assaults, especially revered by Slayers who have sworn their oaths.
Grungni is the god of mining and smithing, father of the Dwarf race, who taught the Dwarfs how to unearth and shape the metals hidden within the earth.
Morgrim is the god of engineering, the first engineer to teach the Dwarf clans how to craft devices, machines, and engines of war.
The greatest Runesmiths joined forces with the Engineers' Guild to create these tireless sentinels - such a wonder is both a pride of the past and an echo of sorrow.
The greatest Runesmiths joined forces with the Engineers' Guild to create these tireless sentinels - such a wonder is both a pride of the past and an echo of sorrow.
The greatest Runesmiths joined forces with the Engineers' Guild to create these tireless sentinels - such a wonder is both a pride of the past and an echo of sorrow.
These colossal guardians are inscribed with runes said to have been forged by Grungni himself amid rolling thunder - draw too close, and be charred to cinders.
Rune Guard (Multi-Barrel Rune Gun)
Valaya created runes, oaths, grudges, and Dwarven culture, presiding over healing, unity, and the hearth - she is also the Dwarfs' goddess of brewing.

Every Blade-Reaper warband answers to a bloodthirsty champion who claims skulls not for themselves, but for their wrathful master. Though they may appear as mere handlers of the war-hounds within the Blood Hunt's ranks, the Blade-Reapers themselves track different quarry. Unlike hounds, a Blade-Reaper understands how mortal prey think, and can deduce their intentions - a feat the flesh hounds could never achieve.
Each Blade-Reaper warband is led by a blood-crazed fiend clad in blood-soaked heavy armor, wielding brazen daemon blades, calmly deliberating before savagely claiming the skulls of the weak.
How can blood possibly be crushed? Well, with an axe so massive you can't see its edge, this bunch of enormous fools are truly mad enough to try.
Rather than sacrifice a dragon's skull, the Blood God prefers to brand his burning sigil upon its draconic soul, binding an eternal will to it.

Karanak's fearsome lieutenants are all bloodthirsty fiends from the Unfettered Fury Legion. They know they have suffered failure in Khorne's eyes, but the Blood Hunt offers them a chance to reclaim their lost glory.
A Chaos Warrior brave enough must endure a grueling ritual, repeatedly piercing the beast with a magical blade, in order to subdue this colossal creature of bloody madness.
The souls of cowards are trapped within these daemonic constructs; their only worth lies in serving as fuel for the forging of hellish flame.
Nothing pleases the God of War more than skulls—if one skull can be traded for even more skulls, then prepare for a promotion!
The Snow Eagle wheels through the sky, ice arrows nocked upon its bow, as a storm descends from the heavens.
Only the bravest warriors of the Guard may earn the title of Golden Knight retainer - each Golden Knight retainer is granted a newly-forged suit of gleaming enchanted armour.

The frost court can forge millennia-old ice into armour both light and unyielding, which the Tzarina bestows upon her Ice Guard and their mighty war bears - sisters riding to war and loosing arrows, what splendid valor!

Following the Tsarina's reforms, the Kreml Guard still uphold the tradition of wearing black armor. Standing at the very front line against Chaos, their specialized duck-foot pistols leave the northmen with no room to advance.

The Kreml Guard still uphold the tradition of wearing black armor, but now they stand at the front line against Chaos bearing sturdy halberds. Their flammable kvass can turn the battlefield into a sea of fire.

In the era of the Red Tsarina, some members of the Kreml Guard traveled to Erengrad to study the marksmanship of the Streltsi. They can wield firearms with pinpoint accuracy and swing long-handled war axes with equal ease.
Taming a bad-tempered elk is no less difficult than forging a bond with the Bear God's offspring, but clad in heavy armor, their charging formation can stir up a blizzard of its own.
When you hear the elk's cry, turn and flee unless you wish to be trampled underfoot—that is the vengeance of Kislev's frozen incarnation!
Massive and powerful elk roam the northern borders of Kislev. Capturing this species is exceedingly difficult, but their boundless endurance and strength make it all worthwhile.
Dazh is the god of fire and the sun. Molten gold pours over surging lava elementals, and as flames rise, all impurity is burned away.
Salyak is the goddess of healing and comfort. She condenses the elements of life into a divine statue; her sturdy wooden form bears miracles, like a white bird of early spring bringing hope of life.

Tor is the god of thunder and warriors, his massive oaken axe splitting the sky. He calls down colossal beings formed of lightning elementals, letting enemies feel the thunder of high summer firsthand.
A statue of the Bear God stands atop a massive construct of ice and frost, master of the cold and death; Kislev's fate is bound to the favour of Ursun.
The Ungol people excel at raising Snow Eagles. As war smoke rises along the borderlands, these sharp-eyed hunters seek out enemies from a thousand leagues away.
Great beasts prowl the dense forests of the provinces, while ice-winged leopards weave and wheel through the sky, tormenting all who witness their terrible frost with dread.
A cunning creation of the Changer of Ways, displaying the full might of magic in all its glory.
The greatest art the God of Pleasure believes he has ever crafted—it drags all upon the battlefield into a nameless realm of illusion.
The Blood God's daemon engine spews forth flames of Khorne, bringing death upon the mortal world.
Bin-iron warriors bear dragonflame; ten thousand chariots break the enemy line, leaving only wreckage behind.
Long halberds reap the enemy like grain; iron hooves thunder through the mist.
Drifting clouds obscure the sun, the dragon's fury shakes the heavens; sails catch the wind and carry them a thousand li in an instant.
Four Divine Beasts, you are but songstresses! Zhao Ming, unleash the Dragon Transformation and kick him to death!
In the dim glow of green lanterns, they guide the fallen home; those who disturb the long wall shall have their souls returned upon the spirit banner.
Flame-forged terracotta warriors man the cannons that guard the dragon gate, their thunder shaking the world.
Axe and halberd gleam beneath the sun, guarding heaven's gate; trespassers shall be cut down.
Forged from ink jade into terracotta form, their divine arms draw the bow, arrows swifter than shooting stars.
[Soul Dragon] Shi Yan Mo guides the spirits of Cathay's fallen, traveling between the two realms; should the long wall face grave peril, he sends his avatar's soul to descend upon the battlefield.
The jade sea dragon turtle bears the fortress upon its back, fire arrows and bullets falling like rain; only overwhelming numbers dare approach it.
Mo Dao sabers cut down man and horse alike; forming a wall, they hold the line unbreakable.
Hawk eyes track the enemy's trail; long rifles pierce the target a hundred paces away.
Feathered shafts blot out the sun like a swarm of locusts, while sturdy shields ward off the enemy.
Dark armor black as ink, cold blade white as snow; ink flame rises with every strike, cutting down evil and breaking every technique.
Disciples of the Jade Blood Taoist temple possess the sharp senses of serpents and unmatched beauty, only emerging into the world when summoned by the Jade Court.
The heroic spirits of generals drive forth in jade armor, their bodies forming a wall against every evil.
Once carefree amid the bamboo sea, but now calamity has risen among demons; trampling bone and devouring iron was never their wish, only that all under heaven find peace.
Patrolling beyond the wall, scouting the enemy's vanguard, hawk rifles bring death to their foes.
Thunder crashes with the dragon's wrath; jade-clad riders hurl flame and bring death in their wake.
Eyes bright as stars, arrows piercing the vast sky—death falls from the heavens.
Guardians of the Dragon Emperor, proud above all heroes, their glory illuminates the realm.
No rope has ever crossed its nose; heaven and earth are its only pen, and by night it never rests.
In a single night the wind and fire of candlelight rose, spreading ninety thousand li across the Tian Shan.
Forth from the Tian Shan they came, razing courts and sweeping dens, scattering blood and bone, sealing the wolf at Xu Lang.
Kroxigors of greater "wisdom" can fight docilely alongside Skinks, tearing through enemy lines with far greater efficiency.
Yokamado Zatt and Ta'grath
This is the descent of the Sun God's will. Lizardmen who behold it are reinvigorated with new vitality, and even their weapons take on the radiance of the blazing sun.
The stars...foresee...the ancient foe returns...I...shall hold them back...the demon spawn...once more.
The God of the Sea once walked through Itza, granting the emerald pools their mighty healing power, and now this blessing turns toward the jungle battlefield.
Tepok granted this strange Carnosaur the instinct to command the Wind of Aethyr; the twin-tailed Oracle astride it will channel the vast power of the heavens.
Great Saurus warriors, upon death, are wrapped in the shrouds bestowed by the War God, continuing to protect their Mage-Priests and kin.
These frighteningly massive Ogres have proven their worth time and again on hunting parties, always ready to hoist their fishbladder launchers and let loose a shot.
If an enemy can truly feel the heat of erupting magma firsthand, then in the eyes of the Firebelly's disciples, this is the Volcano God's most generous reward!
Beneath the deserts of Araby lie the remains of colossal war elephants, and an eternal curse has brought these behemoths back into the light of day.
Unfurl the mighty wings woven from suffering souls, and scatter the Death God's gift down from the heavens!
Tomb Guards equipped with fine halberds and sturdy shields patrol the deepest reaches of the desert, cutting down any uninvited intruder.
Listen to this whisper from the underworld—the Lord of the Dead calls out with a hunger for souls.
Awakened Skeleton Warriors, spears in hand, ride swift and nimble Bone Ostriches in search of their enemies' fatal weaknesses.
The kingdoms of Nehekhara often carved beetles into colossal stone statues, hoping the eternal scarab would forever watch over and protect their people.
Scarabs bearing the names and likenesses of the gods are typically adorned in solid gold, granting them extraordinary magic resistance.
A guardian slumbering in the deepest tomb of the Black Pyramid, forged by the hand of a legendary Liche High Priest—only a scarce few know of this terrible existence.
Heroic spirits chosen by Djaf wield colossal blades engraved with the War God's name; every arc they carve slices a path of blood through the enemy ranks.
The chosen warriors of Ptra are enigmatic and unknowable; their exquisite yet devastating firearms from Cathay can cripple the enemy from afar.
Slumbering for centuries within Asterai's tomb, these colossal statues carved with the visage of the Crocodile God still stand guard around the Hierotitan.
Nagash's most faithful servant, wielding the purest and mightiest necromantic power.
Arkhan's staff draws forth the vast dark magic within the Black Ark, unleashing the power that Nagash left within it.
Asaph's blessing kindled the Warrior Queen's vengeful desire, which ultimately became a cold, venomous bite upon her bowstring.
Though the Tomb High Priest was exiled, the Mortuary Cult's contributions to Nehekhara have earned Ptra's favor.
The Undying Emperor, King of Kings! He bows to no man, and serves only as master!
Ptra's most exalted gift—the golden form and supreme power the Undying Emperor has long dreamed of.
The souls of Tomb Princes are unyieldingly strong; the favor of the gods allows them to take the form of great lions and command their legions.
The faces of Tomb Princes are engraved upon colossal Ushabti, and from them one can feel nothing but ruin.
Ah, yes... the blood-soaked hand...

The mutated body of the Deep Sea Dragon is long and sinuous, its limbs stout yet powerfully muscled, allowing it to move with considerable speed both in the sea and on land. They recover swiftly from wounds, and an endless hunger drives them in a ceaseless search for food, while their mighty tail propels them through the ocean depths - a formidable weapon capable of shattering castle walls. In battle, crushing darkness and bone-deep cold surround them.
The most crazed slaughtering souls are sealed within statues to please the God of the Bloody Hand—both devout and pitiable, yet none can deny their strength.
Asaph's curse caused the most powerful medusas to sprout blood-red wings; the goddess of desire mockingly restored their ability to cast spells while sealing away their limbs and serpents.
The manticore's strength and savagery make it a peerless instrument of slaughter, ridden by noble Black Tower knights as though they were incarnations of Khaine himself.
Deep sea dragons enslaved by the Dark Elves have been infused with the vile magic that permeates the Black Arks, twisting them into forms better suited to hunting in the deep.
Centuries ago, the daemon Tzarkan was imprisoned in Kul Hadar, only to be unwittingly freed by Darkblade; from then on his fate was inescapably entwined with that of the Devourer of Worlds.
Morathi crafted a mutation formula reviled by the world from medusa bone, viscera, souls, and dark magic—but only the most devout of madwomen can claim the greatest power, can they not?
The medusa's face is bound by a cursed mask, infused with endless pain, torment, regret, and despair; a single glance at their vicious eyes will make blood spray from every pore of your body.
Infusing devastating dark energy into a Hydra's endless vitality, then binding its restless power within magically forged armor—this is the wondrous creation of Hekarti, Queen of the Hydras.
The Black Ark is the Druchii's colossal floating fortress of war, its black towers like fingers reaching toward the sky—everything beyond the horizon will be consumed in flame.

The Lothern Sea Guard are ever accompanied by the Skycutter, a magnificent aerial chariot warded by magic and drawn into battle by swift-winged birds. The Sea Guard's bows pose a threat to smaller foes, though the crew prefer the hawk-eye bolt thrower, whose steel bolts, launched with a great rushing wind, can bring down even the mightiest of beasts. Such a valuable weapon is mounted upon the prow of the Skycutter, ensuring the Sea Guard maintains relentless firepower against the enemy once battle is joined.
The Pegasus Hunters of Ellyria wield spears and longbows crafted from night-elm wood, enchanted timber strong enough to shield its bearer from even the darkest sorcery.

Clad in golden armour, the Dragon Princes represent Caledor's mightiest champions - their dragon-fire lances char to cinders all who bar their path, and they draw blade to cut down foes after the charge.
Even facing overwhelming odds, regardless of the enemy's identity or peril, the White Lion Riders hold fast their courage and charge with unbroken pride.
The wondrous flying fish of Cothique's skies are said to be a miracle of Mathlann; the glow from their heads guides lost sailors back to a warm harbor.
Should the Skycutters encounter the enemy unexpectedly, their goal is to eliminate every foe in the air, ensuring the elven forces hold absolute air superiority.
The fallen heroic spirits of Yvresse can return to the mortal world through the power of waystones, clad in golden enchanted armor, illuminating the eternal mist through will and strength alone.
These great lions bearing dreamlike wings are regarded as gifts from Lyahga; to tame one is solid proof of the rider's fearless heart and unbreakable will.
The elves of Nagarythe, locked in eternal vengeance, often pray to the Goddess of Fate and Death; the bloody flocks of ravens stand as proof that this old crone lends her aid.
Avelorn was the first stop where the roots of the World Tree spread into Ulthuan, and under the careful tending of generations of Everqueens, mighty guardian Treemen were born.
Avelorn was the first stop where the roots of the World Tree spread into Ulthuan, and under the careful tending of generations of Everqueens, mighty guardian Treemen were born.

A powerful Saphery mage channels the power of Qhaysh to lift a chunk of earth into the sky, gaining control over the entire battlefield's vision and raining devastating spells down upon the enemy from above.

As the Lord of Athel Loren awakens from his death-mimicking slumber and the horn of the Wild Hunt echoes across the wilds, Kurnous's chosen offer their finest sacrifice to the eternal glory of the Forest King.

Bound by the pull of the Wind of Life, the Zoat and the Thorn Sisters share a wondrous kinship - together they gladly rouse thorn and vine to impale intruders, or reduce them to fertilizer for Athel Loren.
You have indeed seen a towering wall in your dreams, haven't you—a green hell coated in venom and thorns, one you would never wish to approach.
These ancient dryads are reborn from flame, their souls holding an unwavering devotion to Athel Loren; even the most sincere elven oaths pale in comparison.
The ley lines are the web connecting all life and death; these great warriors guard the ley line nodes with near-eternal vigilance, sparing no cost to maintain the balance of souls.
Dying forest spirits bind their souls to corrupted Asrai, and endless whispers gradually merge the two, giving birth to these pitiable yet powerful beings.

They are the most mysterious and dreadful of the Sisters of Thorn; any who dare approach them without leave will be set ablaze by vile moonfire arrows and left to scream out their final moments impaled amid the thorny woods.

The Lord of Athel Loren awakens from his death-like slumber; as the horn of the Wild Hunt sounds across the wilderness, Kurnous's chosen offer the finest sacrifice to the eternal glory of the Forest King.
Not even the fiercest flames can destroy this ancient oak spirit; it has weathered every season's trials, and the spectral souls within the ancient waystone constantly remind it of its duty.

The forest's own resentment naturally gives rise to such a creature of icy, malevolent heart; it moves as gracefully as a perfect dancer, but its twisted branches excel at piercing hearts from behind.

The Willow Spirit is the herald of spring's return, a wellspring of life, and a resting place for departed souls; it can sustain the Wood Elves and forest spirits against even the most terrible of conditions.

Tempered by year upon year of thunderstorms, the Poplar Spirit possesses a body like forged silver and extraordinary vitality, able to channel terrifying thunder that pierces through all armor and flesh.
No matter when winter finally recedes, the indomitable Birch Spirit silently watches over Athel Loren, waiting for all dormant life to be reborn from the ashes.
The Dawi Tank, a heavy war machine of the dwarfs.
An important invention of Torrent Pass, one shot and it's ashes to ashes.
The dwarf mortar, quite capable at killing.
In the War of Vengeance, the elves received plenty of love from the airships.
Elite airship.
Elves play with spears too?
The mightiest spear-wielding warriors of the World's Edge Mountains.
Real accurate—or so the goblins usually say.
The Longbeards got themselves new weapons!
Who're you calling an Ironbreaker Knight! *scoffs*
One swing of the hammer, a lifetime settled.
That bear's kind of huge.
Bang!
Effectively halts enemy advances.
Organ Gun.
Volley Gun.
The Crank Gunners specialize in suppressive fire.
Thunderers dabbling in melee combat, off the beaten path.
The Chaos Dwarfs call these fellows 'Fireglaive gunners.'
Mountain Rangers.
A new weapon—really, this is not a mortar.
Vengeance! Vengeance! Vengeance!
Mighty dwarf sappers, capable of deploying all manner of mechanical devices on the battlefield.
For breaking up soil. Goblin: ...huh?
Mighty broad-axe firearms that can vaporize any enemy.
Bound by both the King's Oath and the Slayer's Oath.
Big caliber—brace yourself.
Steam billowing, engine roaring, this cannon-mounted traction locomotive is unmatched in both horsepower and firepower.
Big caliber—brace yourself.
Under Grom's ingenious whims, more and more bizarre contraptions appear on the battlefield, leaving behind either clouds of dust and flying debris, or splattered blood and gore in red and green.
The fire daemon wields a great glaive, incinerating any foe bold enough to charge before it.
The K'daai Destroyer is a towering beast, capable of crushing fortifications and mighty creatures alike with its burning claws, leaving nothing but ash in its wake.
A K'daai bound to a form that despises the world takes the shape of a colossal bull or minotaur, its charge powerful enough to flatten a hillside.
The K'daai Destroyer bears a pair of massive brass wings, sorcerously blessed and infused with the blood of great sacrificial bulls offered to the Dark Father Hashut.
Its body bristling with spikes and blades, any foe who dares engage it in melee is highly likely to be shredded to ribbons.

Gu Kahn delights in clashing with infantry, charging back and forth through swarms of enemies, scattering their limbs and flesh like splashes of water... and when facing a foe worthy of the name, it turns to technique - a fighting style of its own devising that wields brute force with far greater efficiency.

Gu Ke Jia loves to challenge foes large enough to be worthy - the bigger, the better: snapping a Carnosaur's neck, tearing open a Stegadon's shell, dragging a dragon from the sky and rending it apart, shattering a giant's knee before smashing through its jaw. Gu Ke Jia delights in wielding and displaying its own brute strength, endless brute strength!

Gu Kahn delights in clashing with infantry, charging back and forth through swarming enemy hosts, scattering limbs and flesh like splashing water... yet when facing a truly worthy foe, it turns to technique—a fighting style it has honed itself, one that channels brute strength ever more effectively.

Gu Ke Jia loves to challenge foes as large as possible—the bigger the better: snapping a Carnosaur's neck, tearing open a Stegadon's shell, dragging a dragon from the sky and ripping it apart, shattering a giant's knee before smashing through its jaw—Gu Ke Jia delights in wielding and displaying its own brute strength, endless brute strength!

Xuan Lie stands foremost among the Dragon-Blooded, a descendant of [Lord of Raging Gale] Miao Ying and among those Dragon-Blooded closest in lineage to the true dragon offspring. By right he should command the power to summon wind and rain and breathe cloud and mist, but from a young age, most of his overflowing magical power was not channeled into spellcasting - instead, uncontrolled, it turned toward another purpose: tempering and strengthening his body, making his physical form even mightier than the great dragon elders who soar the skies, and drawing him closer to the soldiers he must lead and protect.\\nAt Miao Ying's behest, for centuries Xuan Lie served under Zhao Ming, Lord of Shang Yang, becoming a cherished confidant in his eyes. The generals of Wei Xi bow before his might without exception, including the self-assured Xiao Xiao, who fell noticeably short when measured against him in trials of skill. Now, with strange portents stirring, Xuan Lie has been charged with holding Wei Nan Province, leading his soldiers to crush the schemes and ambitions of petty villains.
Xuan Lie stands foremost among the Dragon-Blooded of the 'Soaring Dragon' line, possessing valor unmatched by ten thousand men and strength beyond the Four Symbols themselves.

The prototypes of these war machines trace back to the prospecting boom of the Golden Age, but as waves of engineers and miners were swallowed by the green tide, they too were buried deep beneath the rubble - until recent excavations brought them back into the light. Now, survivors of that great calamity mount these refurbished, mass-produced machines, ready to settle accounts with the greenskins and rodent scum alike.

Halfdan Thorsson is a grizzled Gospodar veteran who has faced every manner of foe on the battlefield and lived to tell of it. In the third year of Kislev's endless winter, his company found itself embroiled in an unprecedented, brutal battle, and as he lay dying, a lightning-wreathed warhammer fell from the sky, driving back the Norscan raiders who had surrounded him and rousing him from the brink of unconsciousness brought on by blood loss. Wielding this hammer, he led his company to break free of the Chaos warband's encirclement.\\nHe then embarked upon a trial of self-testing: annihilating the warband of Sorem the Clamorous, freeing slaves aboard a Dark Elf pirate ship, felling a mercenary giant with his bare hands, and winning a drinking contest set by the Dwarfs, among other feats. From these trials he emerged bearing his trophies: a suit of armour forged by a Dwarf Runesmith, a warhammer imbued with the power of Thor and reinforced with a haft of forest-spirit wood, and an exquisite winged Dwarf helm - a keepsake of his fallen friend. Halfdan took the name '[Son of Thor]' and returned to the lands of the Motherland as a chosen champion of the god.
This battle-hardened Kossar veteran earned Thor's favor at the brink of death, and having completed his trial, he now returns to Kislev as a chosen warrior, continuing to fight for the Motherland.

Among the ancient Kroxigor there are rare specimens born larger and more powerfully built than their kin, fiercer and mightier still. Rather than laying the foundation stones of temples, they excel at eliminating potential threats lurking near the temple grounds, and through millennia of battle they have earned the honor of bearing arms and armour left behind by the Old Ones. They shall continue to serve as the Old Ones' vanguard, clearing every obstacle before the Great Plan.

A colossal beast built from bones and blazing fire, bearing the Blood God's oracle as it leads maddened followers trudging through blood and mud, leaving scorched bones and severed limbs strewn in its wake.
These rare and ancient Kroxigors are the last survivors of the spawning pools, bearing sacred arms left behind by the ancients, born only to crush all who stand in the way of the Great Plan.
Earth, wind, fire, water—this compass is our decree; it drives the thunder and grips the lightning, faithfully obeying the emperor's command.
Older fire salamanders bear thick, deep-green scales; only the most trusted skink handlers may approach without fear of their dreadful venomous flame.
Ogres who aspire to feast on dragon meat trace Dwarf Slayers' fire-resisting runes onto their limbs in blood, then charge straight into the fiercest flames to test the results.
The Gnoblars most favored by the tyrant arm themselves as thoroughly as they can, especially protecting their spindly arms—after all, no one in the tribe is short enough to grab their legs.
These cooks are skilled at turning the Ogres' leftover bone scraps and rotting meat into "rations" to feed their kin. The stench is so overpowering that they must wear nose guards while cooking.
The relatively clever Gnoblars often scrounge together a suit of scrap metal to protect themselves—which makes for a fine can of preserved food for a Sabretusk!
Frostwolves have a sense of smell and agility to rival Sabretusks, and every Gnoblar tries to convince their hulking master to tame one—mostly so they can run away faster!
These scrawny little arms and legs hardly matter, but since they can pound the enemy into mincemeat, it's still quite the bargain—saves us the trouble of chewing!
The Frost Mammoth possesses a chill to rival the Thundertusk itself; this colossal beast is in itself an excellent living larder and food reserve for the tribe.
To become a master Leadbelcher, one must survive bare-handed among a pack of ferocious Sabretusks; the finest masters usually come away with the toughest hides.
The tenderest meat on a Frost Mammoth can freeze an Ogre's teeth right off, while its remaining icy bones can hack a man into shards of frost.
These merciless sentinels lurk beneath the yellow sands, watching over the domain of the goddess Asaph. The sandstorms they raise will sweep away anyone bold enough to gaze upon her.
Engine normal, gauges normal... the size of the rats charging this way, not so normal.
Thicker armor, stronger power, a stubborn pilot—the Steam Fist is charging up!
Engines roaring, gun barrels preheating—tear the charging rats into rags!
Rat scum! Just try touching my Steam-Dial Machine!

These creations, cobbled together from twisted flesh and grotesque machinery, are shared property of Clan Pestilens and Clan Skryre. The horrifying experiments performed upon them repeatedly push past the limits of how much warpstone can be embedded and how thoroughly flesh can be fused with machine, and their rampaging, mowing presence on the battlefield stands as the finest advertisement either clan could ask for.
The supreme masterwork of Clan Pestilens and Clan Skryre, its flesh embedded with warpstone and killing machinery far beyond what any grotesque creation should be able to bear.

Clan Skryre have mounted an endlessly spinning drill upon this mound of twisted flesh; as it bores through even the sturdiest fortress gates, warpstone shards drenched in magic scatter endlessly into the air.
This monster, its body filled with warpstone fuel, can spew forth a torrent of massive green warpflame; warpstone is its very source of life, like an ever-burning, inexhaustible heart of fire.
Crimson-patterned gold armor, silent across the desert; the fire steed's neigh shatters the enemy's courage, candle-flame consuming both life and death.
Encased in inches-thick steel armour, this Chaos Giant is slower and clumsier than before, yet ordinary ranged weapons can do nothing against this half-mad living weapon.
Legend tells of the mysterious Ten Palaces of Sha Xu beneath the Soul River, guarded by a colossal turtle whose dark armor stands unbreakable and unassailable when it holds firm.

Hong Ying was born on the streets of Fu Zhou, never knowing his parents, surviving as a drifter among the wharves and markets. In this chaotic world he displayed astonishing gifts - the deceptions of merchants, the schemes of sailors, the corruption of officials, all laid bare before his eyes as if written on paper. At the age of seven, a Black Jade Crow Warden dispatched to oversee the Fu Zhou markets discovered that the blood flowing through Hong Ying's veins belonged to the long-thought-extinct Shadow Dragon bloodline. Upon hearing this, the Moon Empress herself descended in avatar to receive him. Within the Twin Moon Garden, the Moon Empress personally washed the grime from his body, bestowed upon him the name Hong Ying, and taught him the arts of combat, espionage, and the mastery of dragon blood.\\nOn the eve of the Moon Empress's and the Dragon Emperor's disappearance, the Moon Empress issued a divine edict establishing the Cassia Confidants in her name. Gui Po - the dark side of the moon. The Cassia Confidants answer to no court or ministry, reporting directly to Yu An Bo, the overseer appointed by the Moon Empress. Its mission: to watch over all of Cathay, infiltrate enemy ranks, suppress rebellion, and protect the people of the Celestial Empire. Hong Ying, sole heir to the Shadow Dragon bloodline, was appointed by the Moon Empress as the first Overseer of the Cassia Confidants.\\nThe relationship between Hong Ying and Yu An Bo is one of both lord and vassal, and comrades in arms - Yu An Bo presides from the Jade Court, orchestrating strategy with unmatched wisdom, while Hong Ying moves through the shadows, sensing the pulse of every corner of the Empire through the reach of the Cassia Confidants. Yu An Bo's assessment of Hong Ying is but a single sentence:\\n"I know all there is to know of Cathay, because Hong Ying has seen it all for me." Between them they have forged Cathay's most secretive and effective intelligence network: Yu An Bo handles decision-making and coordination, Hong Ying handles execution and infiltration. The hidden agents of the Cassia Confidants span every corner, from the frontier passes of the Long Wall to the southern jungles, from the trade roads of the western regions to the islands of the eastern sea. No conspiracy can hide from Hong Ying's gaze for more than three days.

Liu Wang Que was born into the prestigious Liu clan of Shang Wu, a family that had for generations overseen the Jade Court's astronomical charts and royal library. From childhood she displayed a gift beyond the ordinary: not only did she never forget what she read, but she could discern cause and effect from the barest traces of evidence. At the age of twelve, using nothing but palace rumors and fragments of correspondence, she pieced together the full picture of a conspiracy by followers of Tzeentch to commit treason - though this feat was not without cost. The Tzeentch cultists, in their dying moments, struck back at the Liu household, taking her parents' lives and leaving her left eye with a wound that would never fully heal. This incident caught even the Jade Dragon's attention, who personally arranged for Liu Wang Que to study within the Scripture Repository.\\nWhen Hong Ying, acting on the Moon Empress's command, formed the Cassia Confidants, he personally called upon the Liu family and invited Liu Wang Que to serve as his deputy. Hong Ying asked her: 'There is one thing I do not understand - the Moon Empress's edict speaks of Gui Po. What is Gui Po?' Liu answered: 'The moon waxes and wanes; Gui Po is the dark side of the moon. The Celestial Empire of Cathay needs soldiers who stand in the light, but it also needs those who watch from the shadows.' Upon hearing this, Hong Ying knew that Liu had already grasped the Moon Empress's true intent, and sincerely appointed her as his deputy overseer.\\nHong Ying and Liu Wang Que complement one another in temperament: Hong Ying is decisive and incisive, while Liu Wang Que is composed and meticulous. Liu Wang Que oversees the daily operations of intelligence: planting informants, decoding ciphers, interrogating traitors, and directing covert agents. Calm and precise, she rarely lets emotion show, and her subordinates address her as Lady Wang Que - a title both of respect and quiet awe. Under her stewardship, the intelligence network of the Cassia Confidants transformed from a rough, sprawling web into a tightly woven net without a single gap. Hong Ying can confidently venture to the front lines and undertake the most perilous missions, for he knows - Liu Wang Que holds the rear guard, and the moonlight of the Cassia Confidants will never go dark.

[Moonlight Edict] Liu Wang Que and Hong Ying are both superior and subordinate, and confidants as well. Hong Ying handles external affairs, overseeing the overall situation and diplomatic maneuvering; Liu Wang Que manages internal matters, ensuring the intelligence network remains airtight.
